Kilkenny County Council Reduce Your Use Campaign 
Kilkenny County Council’s Reduce Your Use campaign 
has been a great success. The campaign (October 2023 to 
March 2024) consisted of promoting energy efficiency 
within the organisation with a particular focus on the 
Thomastown and Callan Area Offices.  
 
Reduce your Use is a joint initiative of SEAI and the 
Office of Public Works which supports public bodies to 
run a winter energy awareness and energy reduction 
programme. The target is 15% energy reduction. The 
Kilkenny County Council project achieved 24% energy 
reduction in two buildings in the Callan/Thomastown 
MD.  This was achieved with a combination of 
behavioural change and a small investment in energy 
reduction measures. A video and interactive report 
which documents the campaign will be available on the 
Council website and promoted in early May.  
 
ENVIRONMENTAL AWARENESS 
 
Litter Management Plan 
The public consultation process for the Litter Management Plan 2024 – 2026 closed on 15th March 2024 and 
on the 22nd April 2024, the Litter Management Plan 2024 – 2026 was approved by the Plenary. 
 
 
 
Tree Care Webinar 
Aoife Munn, a horticulturist completed a one hour webinar on the 1st of May and give tips on how to 
improve your tree care skills. Topics included staking, tree tie management, mulching, watering, pruning, 
and protecting young trees from pests and diseases.  This was a collaborative project undertaken by the 
Environmental Awareness Officer, the Biodiversity Officer and Heritage. 
 
Air Quality Campaign 
In conjunction with the Enforcement Team in Environment, the EAO is coordinating a targeted campaign 
throughout the city and county on air quality and the continued use of smoky coals. The campaign seeks to 
raise awareness amongst the wider public, stakeholders, businesses and schools about the health and 
environmental impacts of poor air quality and the ways individuals can help reduce pollution. This will be 
a 4-6 week campaign commencing the week of the 15th of April 2024.

Anti-Litter and Anti-Graffiti Grant 2024 
Kilkenny County Council is offering community groups an opportunity this year to promote anti- litter and 
anti-graffiti awareness in their local community.  The grant is to mobilize community groups to care for 
their local environment by decreasing the impact of litter by its removal and to promote a social message 
locally to encourage everyone to put litter in its rightful place – in a bin. 
 
As funding comes directly from the Department of Communications, Climate Action & Environment there 
are funding restrictions which must be adhered to. 
 
This grant cannot cover:  
 
▪ 
the purchase structural items such as street furniture 
▪ 
the purchase of litter bins 
▪ 
the purchase of dog bag dispensers  
▪ 
the purchase of signage 
▪ 
the purchase or rental of CCTV cameras  
 
The grant can cover expenses such as: 
 
▪ 
The purchase of bags for dog bag dispensers if dispensers are already installed at are under the care 
of the group 
▪ 
The expense of litter disposal resulting from litter picks and the expense of disposal of rubbish from 
public street bins which are under the guardianship of the community group 
▪ 
Awareness events highlighting the issue of litter and dog fouling in your local community 
 
The application process will open on Monday 8th of April and applications can be accessed via our website: 
Environment - Kilkenny County Council (kilkennycoco.ie) or by contacting Deirdre.trait@kilkennycoco.ie.  
Deadline for applications is the 24th of May, 2024.  
 
Team Up to Clean Up-Together for Kilkenny 
 
 
The formal launch of the “Team Up to Clean Up-Together for Kilkenny” will take place on the week of the 
27th of May, 2024. An online portal will open for registrations on Monday 27th of May.  
 
This year’s “Team Up to Clean Up” will take place on the 20th-22nd of September.  
Kilkenny has a wow factor that is the envy of other Irish counties. Kilkenny City is recognised nationally as 
a litter free location, regularly winning medals in the IBAL and Tidy Towns competitions and even being 
awarded the much-coveted title of overall Tidy Towns national winner on two occasions. 
 
The County-Wide Clean Up initiative brought together residents, businesses, and local organizations to 
collaborate in a mass effort to enhance the cleanliness and sustainability of our county.  Last year we saw 
over 200 groups register with over 500 volunteers participate. This culminated in a collection of just over 24 
tonnes of litter.

7 
 
The “Team Up to Clean Up” event created a sense of community ownership and pride by engaging 
participants in a variety of cleanup activities, awareness campaigns, and environmental educational 
programs. It created a sense of ownership and focus for many communities, with significant additional 
interest by many groups and individuals outside of national campaigns such as the annual National Spring 
Clean which takes place during the month of April. All cohorts of society engaged resulting in the “Team 
Up to Clean Up” exemplifying best practice in the areas of social inclusion and environment. 
 
We aim to take this event one step further this year by investing in the next generation of stewards through 
the Green Schools Programme and developing a series of education and awareness workshops.

Bring Banks Usage 
The Council provides and manages 46 Bring Centers across the City and County.  A total of 684 tonnes of 
recyclables were collected from our Bring Centers so far in 2024.  This represents that the 1% decreased to 
the prior year during the same period. Aldi - Kilkenny city (16 tonnes collected), Lidl - Johnswell, Kilkenny 
City (13 tonnes collected), Loughboy shopping center - Kilkenny City (12 tonnes collected), and are the 
busiest locations in the City. Aldi - Ferrybank (8 tonnes collected), Lidl - Thomastown (8 tonnes collected) 
and Aldi - Callan (7 tonnes collected) are the busiest outside of the city.  Environment staff are continuing 
to work very closely with our service providers to ensure the collection service is in keeping with demand, 
especially around long weekends and holiday periods. 
 
Dunmore Civic Amenity Site 
The Dunmore site continues to provide an excellent and essential service to the greater Kilkenny community 
and has cemented its place as one of Kilkenny County Council’s leading service providers with the addition 
of the Kilkenny Countryside Park on the closed Landfill site. This combined amenity has seen many 
recycling conscious people combine their trip to the Dunmore CAS with a healthy walk in the Countryside 
Park during March 2024.

Water Quality – Farm Inspections 
Inspections are ongoing with regards to Agricultural & Domestic Wastewater Treatment Systems in the 
county in order to reach our RMCEI targets for 2024. We will also be conducting call backs in the coming 
months on inspections carried out in 2023 to ensure issues around non compliances have been rectified.  
A meeting was recently held with the Environment Section of Kilkenny County Council and the Oversight 
& Reporting Team in the EPA for Agricultural Inspections. Various issues were discussed including the 
total number of National Agricultural Inspections that Kilkenny County Council have to complete in 2024 
and reporting requirement for each inspection. A number of new staff are currently being recruited to 
specifically carry out these attentional farm inspections and the training courses are being set up in Gurteen 
Agricultural College next month for staff to get the appropriate training.  
 
Air Quality 
The Environment Section of Kilkenny County Council will start a media campaign with regards to air 
quality in the county and how we can improve it. The burning of fossil fuels releases particulate matter 
emitting an array of pollutants that reduce air quality and harm life, especially Sulphur Dioxide, Nitrogen 
Oxides, and airborne particles such as soot.  
 
In conjunction with the Enforcement Team in Environment, the EAO is coordinating a targeted campaign 
throughout the city and county on air quality and the continued use of smoky coals. The campaign seeks to 
raise awareness amongst the wider public, stakeholders, businesses and schools about the health and 
environmental impacts of poor air quality and the ways individuals can help reduce pollution. This will be 
a 4-6 week campaign commencing the week of the 15th of April 2024.

All Environmental complaints received are logged on the CRM (Customer Relations Management)

illegal dumping.  Whilst every effort is made to bring unacceptable environmental practice into compliance, 
Environment Enforcement staff continue to manage significant enforcement cases progressing through

Millennium Forest - Trail Enhancement and Accessibility Scheme 
A contract was recently awarded to Shay Power Ltd., to carry-out trail enhancement and accessibility works 
in the Millennium Forest just outside the city. This contractor was procured using Coillte’s Works 
Framework. Works are expected to commence in May and will include carpark and entrance enhancements, 
significant upgrading of the existing Green Loop to include 2.1km’s of trail rehabilitation to facilitate 
universal access with a particular focus on wheelchair users. Other works include improvements to the 
longer Red Loop,  the provision of universal and age friendly accessible amenity spaces, delineated disabled 
and age friendly car parking spaces. The wheelchair accessible toilet (Dry loo) which was installed last year 
under this scheme will be opened to the public in tandem with the completion of the overall project, which 
includes an access path to same. Funding of €200,000 to facilitate the above was secured under the ORIS 
Measure 2 and with match funding from the Council’s own resources the completed project will see an 
investment of €227,000 into this public amenity.

Lacken Boardwalk Replacement Scheme  
Following a competitive tender process the works contract for the Lacken Boardwalk Replacement Scheme 
was awarded to Triur Construction Ltd. The recycled plastic component’s for the boardwalk have been 
signed off by the design team and the contractor has ordered same with works expected to commence in 
the coming weeks.  It is noted  to facilitate these works sections of the boardwalk will be closed to the public 
during this period.  
 
The completed project will see the replacement of the existing 1.2m wide timber boardwalk with a c.3.6m 
wide boardwalk made from recycled composite materials. Funding for this project was secured under 
Measure 3 of the Outdoor Recreation Infrastructure Scheme in the amount of €500,000 which will be 
supplemented from the Council’s own funds.

Kilkenny Countryside Park 
The inaugural Kilkenny Junior Park Run took place on Sunday 21st April in the Kilkenny Countryside Park 
at Dunmore. The event was a great success with 175 participants and 26 volunteers in attendance.  This free, 
fun and friendly 2km event, which will be held every Sunday morning, is suitable for children of all abilities 
aged from 4 years to 14 years old. These events offer families the opportunity to get involved and get active 
in the outdoors. Kilkenny County Council are delighted that our new Countryside Park was identified by 
Parkrun Ireland and the local volunteer group as the location for the Kilkenny Junior Park Run, and 
numbers attending to date have been very positive with the expectation the event will grow week on week.

The Library Services have also rolled out their Slí Na Scéalta outdoor family reading experience  in the 
Kilkenny Countryside Park. This fun learning experience, featuring author Brendan McDonalds’s story 
“The Elephant on the Farm”, is displayed across story panels located around the 1.3km accessible trail, so 
you can follow the story from beginning to end as you walk! The trail was previously located within 
Woodstock Gardens and proved very popular with our younger visitors.

Creative Ireland Heritage Office/Library Service 
Programme 
This year marks the 700th Anniversary of the 
Kilkenny Witch Trials, during which Alice 
Kyteler became the first person in Europe to be 
condemned to death for Witchcraft and Petronella 
de Meath became the first person to be burned at 
the stake for witchcraft.  Funded by Creative 
Ireland, the Heritage Office in partnership with 
the Library Service will curate a programme of 
initiatives to commemorate this iconic event in 
our history and will engage a wide audience 
(primarily focused on younger people) in 
creativity and heritage in County Kilkenny 
through this story. This will include author talks, 
an educational resource pack and creative 
workshops for primary school children, history 
workshops for secondary school children, a video 
shorts series for young adults and a witch trial 
tour for the general public.
